items.name: Product traceability regulations
items.version: Varies by industry and jurisdiction (e.g. food safety, medical device, automotive)
items.jurisdiction: Industry- and jurisdiction-specific (e.g. FDA 21 CFR Part 820 for US medical devices, EU Regulation 2017/745 MDR)
items.scope: Requiring forward/backward genealogy of lots and serials from raw material to finished, shippable product, often with defined retention periods.
items.notes: General placeholder for industry/jurisdiction-specific traceability rules. Sector-specific instances are now broken out separately: fda_qmsr_21_cfr_part_820 and eu_mdr_2017_745 for medical devices, and fsma_204_food_traceability for food. Neither cloned source (InvenTree, odoo-mrp) implements a regulation-specific retention or reporting requirement; both provide the underlying genealogy data (StockItemTracking, stock.lot) a compliant process would be built on top of.

provenance.notes: Flagged from the domain brief's guidance on traceability; not verified against a specific regulation's text.

items.name: ISO 9001 quality management
items.version: ISO 9001:2026 (published 2026-09-16, supersedes ISO 9001:2015; certificates to the 2015 edition remain valid during a 3-year transition to 2029-09-30)
items.jurisdiction: Global (voluntary, contractually required by some customers)
items.scope: Documented quality management processes, including inspection records, non-conformance handling, and corrective action.
items.notes: A voluntary certification, not a legal requirement; named here because inspection/non-conformance record-keeping (clauses on release of product, control of nonconforming outputs, and corrective action) is commonly built to support it, not because InvenTree, odoo-mrp, or ERPNext implement or claim certification. Version/date corroborated via multiple secondary sources (ANSI Blog, DNV, DQS, TUV); the primary iso.org page returned HTTP 403 to an automated fetch.

provenance.notes: ERPNext's Non Conformance/Quality Action doctypes are the kind of records ISO 9001 clause 8.7/10.2 audits typically require; not a claim of certification support.

items.name: ISO 10012 measurement management systems
items.jurisdiction: Global (voluntary; often required where calibrated measurement equipment underpins quality inspection records)
items.scope: Requirements for measurement processes and measuring equipment used to demonstrate conformity, including calibration traceability.
items.notes: Relevant wherever quality_inspections relies on calibrated gauges/instruments; not implemented or asserted as supported by any source reviewed this session. Full text not accessed (paywalled, iso.org blocked automated fetch).

provenance.notes: Version/date corroborated via secondary sources (ANSI Blog, Beamex); iso.org itself not fetched.

items.name: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
items.version: Current e-CFR text (in force since 1997; part unchanged in substance)
items.jurisdiction: United States (FDA-regulated industries, e.g. medical device and pharmaceutical manufacturing)
items.scope: Requirements for electronic records and electronic signatures to be considered trustworthy, reliable, and equivalent to paper records/handwritten signatures — relevant to electronic quality-inspection records, non-conformance records, and traceability audit trails when a manufactured product is FDA-regulated.
items.notes: Applies only when the manufactured product is FDA-regulated (e.g. medical devices, pharmaceuticals); not a general manufacturing requirement. Neither cloned source implements audit-trail/signature controls to this standard. Direct ecfr.gov fetch was blocked by the site's bot-protection this session.

provenance.notes: Scope described from well-established public knowledge of the rule; primary text not freshly fetched this session (ecfr.gov blocked automated access).

items.name: FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820)
items.scope: US device current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements, now harmonized with ISO 13485:2016 for medical device quality management systems, superseding the former free-standing Quality System Regulation (QSR) text.
items.notes: Applies only to medical device manufacturers selling into the US. Fetched directly from fda.gov this session. Neither cloned source (InvenTree, odoo-mrp) nor ERPNext implements or claims QMSR/ISO 13485 conformance.

provenance.notes: Fetched directly from the FDA's own page (fda.gov).

items.name: EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) 2017/745
items.jurisdiction: European Union (medical devices placed on the EU market)
items.scope: Requires a Unique Device Identification (UDI) system and forward/backward traceability of devices through the supply chain (Article 27).
items.notes: Applies only to manufacturers placing medical devices on the EU market. Not fetched directly this session (cited from well-established public knowledge of the regulation's UDI/traceability provisions); neither cloned source implements a UDI-specific traceability model.

provenance.notes: Not independently re-fetched this session; scope description not verified against a freshly read primary text.

items.name: FDA Food Traceability Rule (FSMA Section 204)
items.version: 21 CFR Part 1, Subpart S; compliance date extended to 2028-07-20 (originally 2026-01-20)
items.jurisdiction: United States (manufacturers/processors/packers/holders of foods on the FDA Food Traceability List)
items.scope: Requires capturing Key Data Elements (KDEs) at defined Critical Tracking Events (CTEs) across the supply chain and making traceability records available to FDA within 24 hours.
items.notes: Applies only to food manufacturers handling foods on the FDA's Food Traceability List. Not implemented or asserted as supported by InvenTree, odoo-mrp, or ERPNext. Confirmed via WebSearch results linking to fda.gov and federalregister.gov; the FDA page itself was not fetched in full this session.

provenance.notes: Compliance-date extension corroborated via multiple independent secondary sources plus a direct link to fda.gov and federalregister.gov in search results; not independently re-fetched.
